performance.packet-buffer: 16 MB on-chip plus 6 GB deep DRAM buffer

gaps.note: TWO EDGECORE DOCUMENTS GIVE THIS CHASSIS TWO DEPTHS, 61 mm apart. The data sheet (Edgecore AGR100 (AS5912-54X) Data Sheet R20) states 440 x 548 x 44 mm (W x D x H). The quick start guide (AGR100 AS5912-54X Quick Start Guide R02) states 438.4 x 609.0 x 43.25 mm. The difference is not rounding and not a unit conversion: 609.0 mm is 24 inches, and 548.0 is near no round figure in either unit. The model carries the data sheet's 440 x 548 x 44, as `provenance.chassis` says, and rules out the 438.4 x 43.5 of the AS7726 and AS7326 line on purpose. The QSG's 609 mm depth was never recorded until now, so a reader holding the QSG could not tell that the choice was made with it in view.
gaps.wanted: a measured depth, rail to rear, off a real unit - a tape measure settles it, as edgecore/as7946-30xb settled its own 480-versus-524 depth by measuring hardware.

bottom-row-labels.note: 51 and 54 are NOT silkscreened on the unit; drawn dimmed for reference only

chassis.note: datasheet (Dimensions WxDxH 440 x 548 x 44 mm; Weight 9.34 kg). Note this chassis is NOT the 438.4 x 43.5 of the AS7726/AS7326 line - it is 440 x 44

mgmt-leds.note: LNK and ACT, bracketed to the management port between the Mgmt and Console silkscreen lines (IMG_2179)

mgmt-silkscreen.note: an up-arrow Mgmt line over a down-arrow Console line, beneath the RJ45 stack

port-arrangement.note: datasheet Interfaces figure - 48 SFP+ as 2 rows x 24 columns in three visual groups of 8, and 6 QSFP28 as 2 columns x 3 rows

port-numbering.note: read off the unit's silkscreen in the 3D capture. SFP+ pairs read N-up / N+1-down (45 up, 46 down, 47 up, 48 down), so column-major. QSFP is also column-major but NOT contiguous with a row reading - the strip below QSFP row 2 reads '49 up / 50 down' and '52 up / 53 down', which puts the unlabelled bottom row at 51 and 54, not 53 and 54

port-pitch.note: standard - SFP columns on the SFF-8433 basic 14.25, QSFP on the 19.0 measured from TE 2322551-4. Feasibility checks out - 24 x 14.25 = 342 plus 2 x 19.0 = 38 plus the management stack fits the 440mm panel

port-speeds.note: the management jack is `1g`: the datasheet lists one RJ-45 100/1000BASE-T management port (carried in `attrs.management.mgmt-ports`).

qsfp-geometry.note: QSFP row 2 shares its bottom edge with the SFP+ bottom row; the 12.0 and 14.5 row spacings are preserved from the datasheet figure

qsfp-leds.note: between the belly-to-belly pair, per column - up arrow, two round LEDs, down arrow (capture frame 0)

rear-layout.note: datasheet figure (PSU each end, six fans between, numbered 6..1)

rj45-orientation.note: the pair is mirrored with the latch keyways facing AWAY from each other, so the upper jack is the inverted one (IMG_2179)

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 24 SFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-47/port-48), the 2 QSFP pairs (port-49/port-50 and port-52/port-53).

top-bottom-sides.note: from the unit. Bottom label placement, the side-rail vent slots and the rear-corner access panel are from IMG_2178; the top grooves and side venting from the Object Capture frames. Positions are photo-measured, not measured - the chassis outline is the datasheet's 440 x 548 x 44

usb-area.note: the honeycomb stops either side of the USB port - that patch of panel is flat - and the USB trident is printed to its right (owner, from the unit)
